title: DNA Time Stamps Trace the Strawberry's Origins
hook: Jumping bits of DNA leave traces that pile up over time. Researchers read them like time stamps to show the strawberry's genome was built by merging several ancient genomes.
key_points: Transposable elements ('jumping genes') copy themselves to new spots in the genome over time.
Their accumulated traces can act like time stamps, dating events in a genome's past.
Using this, researchers reconstructed the evolutionary history of the strawberry genome.
Modern strawberries were assembled by merging several ancestral genomes — repeated polyploidy.
The method gives a new way to untangle how complex crop genomes came together.
content_html: Strawberries hide a complicated past in their DNA, and researchers have found a new way to read it — by tracking "jumping genes" that leave datable traces behind, reported via ScienceDaily.
extra_html: Transposable elements are stretches of DNA that copy and paste themselves to new spots in the genome. Because fresh copies keep accumulating over time, the pattern they leave behind can work like a series of time stamps. The team used these traces to reconstruct how the strawberry genome was put together — and found it was assembled through multiple ancient genome-merging events, in which whole sets of chromosomes from different ancestors combined (a process called polyploidy). Many of our most important crops carry these doubled or merged genomes, which can add size, vigor, and adaptability. By turning transposable-element traces into a kind of molecular clock, the approach gives researchers a new tool for untangling how complex plant genomes — and the crops we depend on — actually came to be.

related.title: Mutations: When DNA Changes
related.hook: Every time a cell copies its DNA, tiny typos can slip in — most do nothing at all, a few cause disease, and rare ones fuel evolution.

related.title: How New Species Form
related.hook: Split one population in two, let them drift apart long enough, and eventually they can no longer interbreed — that's speciation, the engine that fills the tree of life with branches.

flashcards.prompt: What did the DNA time-stamp method reveal about the strawberry's origins?
flashcards.back_html: That the modern strawberry genome was assembled by merging several ancestral genomes — repeated polyploidy events — rather than descending from a single ancestor.
